target_customer: County and city 911 emergency communications centers (PSAPs) in the US
problem: 911 centers are about 30 percent understaffed while 60 to 80 percent of incoming calls are non-emergencies, leaving dispatchers overloaded.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to public safety agencies (AI call agent AVA and call-taker copilot CORA)

founders.name: Max Keenan
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch: joined YC Summer 2022 building a hair salon booking tool, then pivoted to 911. Background not given in sources opened.

founders.name: James Liu
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no background found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Real time voice AI that must integrate with CAD and phone systems and meet public safety reliability; hard integration work but standard model stack by 2024.

defensibility.rationale: Deep integration with dispatch systems and slow public sector procurement make customers sticky, but voice AI models are widely available.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: By August 2025 TechCrunch named Hyper (6.3 million dollar seed, out of stealth July 2025) and Prepared (founded 2019, added AI voice) as rivals; the CEO claimed Aurelian was the only one live on calls.

market_need_then: At the 2022 batch the company sold salon booking, so 911 need evidence comes from later: a client's parking lot complaint led the CEO to 911 centers; the press release cites 30 percent understaffing nationally.

branding.domain_note: Uses aurelian.com; earlier name Needl (Dealroom lists fka Needl; YC listing needl exists).

identity.mascot_or_character: Named product personas AVA (caller agent) and CORA (call-taker copilot)
identity.voice_and_tone: Supportive of telecommunicators: designed around human judgment, technology extends capacity

rebrands.why: Not stated; Dealroom lists the former name and the pivot occurred after the batch

brand_strength.rationale: Local news coverage of deployments, but no sourced evidence the brand itself drives adoption.

pivots.from: AI appointment booking for hair salons (Needl)
pivots.to: AI call handling for 911 non-emergency lines
pivots.why: TechCrunch says a salon client's blocked parking lot complaint led to 911 centers less than a year after the batch; exact date not given, AI assistant launched May 2024

outcome_analysis: Aurelian entered YC as a salon booking tool, pivoted within a year to answering non-emergency 911 calls, launched in May 2024, and by August 2025 was live in over a dozen centers when it raised a 14 million dollar Series A led by NEA. The wedge is a staffing shortage with measurable call volume savings, with later entrants like Hyper and Prepared now competing. It is active and growing with 45 people.
notes: Competitors empty: as of the 2022 batch the company sold salon booking and no dated 911 AI rivals were found; Hyper and Prepared are recorded in takeover_risk outcome as later entrants. Dealroom lists a seed of 2.5 million dollars in October 2022 at 10 million valuation with YC, Liquid 2, Palm Drive and FUSE; single aggregator source, so unverified and not recorded as a round. Founder education and employers not found. Headquarters Seattle per press release, Houston per VCBacked. Series A confirmed by Business Wire and several outlets.
